title: Ten 2026 Predictions on Which to Hang Your Hat.
subtitle: Out with the old, in with what I believe to be the future.
body_html:
I've got a prediction. I've got a pretty good track record of predictions! Remember when I wrote a whole series of articles about lawsuits coming against employers for breaches of fiduciary duty under ERISA for offering terrible health plans? No, you don’t? I’ll remind you.

The very first article I ever wrote was on this topic:

The department of justice filed a lawsuit against the state of Ohio for violations of EMTALA. This is only the first shot. ERISA is next. The department of labor has already weighed in last week in the state of Massachusetts on fiduciary violations under that statute. Enforcement is coming. This is not a drill.

There was this one in 2022.

Advertisement!

Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment (RAMHT-AI) is coming! Live, and in person.

Get Tickets to RAMHT!

And now, there is a FREE ticket code! It’s at the bottom of the article. January 11th, in San Fran—right in the middle of JPM Health.

Also, to be clear, it’s a big deal to violate ERISA.

Then I wrote the following in 2024:

Every Employer Will Be Sued...Personally

I didn’t imagine it would be all at once. Well, just last week, a whole host of lawsuits were dropped all at once, alleging exactly this kind of fiduciary violation!

Schlichter Bogard Unleashes a New ERISA Suit Genre

It was a classic Schlichter litigation “dump” with suits filed against multiple employers alleging similar violations all on the same day (and, if prior history holds true, this won’t be the last batch). That said, this group included United Airlines, CHS/Community Health Systems Inc., Universal Services of America LP, and Laboratory Corp. of America Holdings.

It also named benefits consultants Gallagher Benefit Services Inc., Mercer Health and Benefits Administration LLC, Lockton Companies LLC, and Willis Towers Watson US LLC[ii] —accusing them of engaging in self-dealing at the expense of participants.

I also predicted the FDA would not approve MDMA-AT. I provided a whole series of arguments in support of that viewpoint.

Can MDMA-AT Be Saved, Part I, Can MDMA-AT Be Saved, Part II, Should MDMA-AT Be Saved, Part III, Saving MDMA from AT: Part IV, Bad Touch!: MDMA Part V, Saving MDMA (and other psychedelic therapies), Part VI, Saving MDMA VII: This Isn’t The First Drug to Have Problems Getting Approved

Thus, in the spirit of seeing the future,

The Frontier Psychiatrists’ 2026 predictions

  1. The first ERISA lawsuit referencing mental health parity violations will be filed.

    1. I have been arguing that this is a good case to bring. It happens in 2026.

  2. AI-Powered Neuromodulation becomes the hot new Venture Funding category.

    1. 2025 saw over $300m invested into neuromodulation health-tech companies, including Radial, Beckley Clinical, Stella Centers, (NRx Subsidiary) Hope Theraputics, and smaller rounds (and pivots) into their SaaS-esque equivalents (Big Leap, Osmind’s Pivot, Everbright). I think 2026 doubles that number into AI-enabled BCI companies, and we will see additional dollars and deal flow into non-invasive devices, too. There is too “little data density for words” on the internet to feed the economic investment into “Big Compute” Data centers. Still, brain output data can power a transformer model just as well.

    2. Look out for news from Merge Labs, Neuralink, and expect Jeff Bezos and maybe even Zuck to have invested in a company in the space. Top-lines from Sanmai, Brainsonix, and other tFUS companies are likely to make news too.

  3. Large-scale trials of Neuromodulation for non-psychiatric indications will start enrolling. Expect Parkinson’s Disease, dystonia, TD, weight loss, and pain associated with general medical conditions to enroll, if not conclude enrollment.

  4. We will have insurance coverage by a national payor—or two—or Accelerated TMS—in the outpatient clinic setting in 2026. It won’t be broad—it will start with pilots and narrow network deals, but the chips will begin to fall.

  5. There will be three or more at-home depression treatment devices on the market by the end of 2026. We already have the Flow approval announced, and more is coming.

  6. Antidepressant prescriptions will drop (globally) for the first time in 2026. This is an ambitious prediction, but I think the zeitgeist and the data are both against these small-molecule drugs.

  7. A professional society for kids’ care (AAP, AACAP, or the like) will issue a warning (or stern guideline) against prescribing all drugs (except prozac) for depression in youth.

  8. COMP360 and KetaFree (IV Ketamine) will be approved for MDD by FDA.

  9. At least two pandemic-era mental-health companies will publicly cease operations— I’m looking at you, fictional DeathStance Health. There will be an additional 2-3 major criminal cases brought against companies selling controlled substances. Done will be convicted all over again.

  10. Everything will be okay enough for most, and the world won’t (literally) end. Hard times will continue for many.

And as a bonus…a long shot, but I’m going to put my dime down.

  1. Alien life will make contact, and we will know we are not alone

See you all in the new year!
